title: HEC-RAS depth and velocity GeoTIFF workflow
text: AOI can SpatVector supported vector path. default crop polygon mask applied. reproducible rectangle selects central part included river sample: Mesohabitat output cropped central area interest. input geometry differs, align = "velocity_to_depth" uses bilinear interpolation project resample continuous velocity depth template. Assigning known missing CRS assume_crs describes existing coordinates; move .
code: e <- terra::ext(h$depth) dx <- terra::xmax(e) - terra::xmin(e) dy <- terra::ymax(e) - terra::ymin(e) aoi <- terra::as.polygons(   terra::ext(     terra::xmin(e) + 0.18 * dx, terra::xmax(e) - 0.18 * dx,     terra::ymin(e) + 0.12 * dy, terra::ymax(e) - 0.12 * dy   ),   crs = terra::crs(h$depth) ) cropped <- classify_mesohabitat_raster(h$depth, h$velocity, aoi = aoi) plot_mesohabitat(   cropped, axes = FALSE, palette = class_colors )

title: hydromeso: fluvial mesohabitat classification in R
text: output depth-velocity hydraulic classification, proof habitat quality fish occupancy. Interpretation depends species life stage, stream type, substrate, cover, connectivity, water quality, temperature, flow regime, hydraulic-model resolution, local validation. Class IDs labels, ordinal scores. Users must decide dry cells represented HEC-RAS model outputs; dry_threshold = NULL preserves exact scheme classifies zero depth zero velocity Class 1. default eight-class table Cordero Harris (Preprint), Semi-Supervised Supervised Machine Learning Approaches Predicting Fluvial Mesohabitats Satellite Data, DOI: 10.2139/ssrn.7100727. broader framework informed Aadland (1993), Stream Habitat Types: Fish Assemblages Relationship Flow, DOI: 10.1577/1548-8675(1993)013<0790:SHTTFA>2.3.CO;2. Source code issue tracking available github.com/el-cordero/hydromeso.

what: hydromeso: Classify Fluvial Mesohabitats from Depth and Velocity — hydromeso-package
title: hydromeso: Classify Fluvial Mesohabitats from Depth and Velocity — hydromeso-package
text: hydromeso applies validated rectangular depth-velocity rules numeric, tabular, vector, raster hydraulic data. default eight-class scheme implements thresholds used Cordero Harris (Preprint), broader depth-velocity mesohabitat framework informed Aadland (1993).

title: hydromeso: Classify Fluvial Mesohabitats from Depth and Velocity — hydromeso-package
text: output hydraulic mesohabitat classification based depth velocity . independently establish biological habitat quality species occurrence. Biological interpretation also depends species, life stage, stream type, substrate, cover, connectivity, water quality, temperature, flow regime, model resolution, local validation. Raster outputs inherit uncertainty hydraulic models input data; alignment interpolation can affect cells near thresholds. Class IDs nominal identifiers rather ordinal scores.
